name: Belarus

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2019: 9475174 inhabitants. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, read through the dissemination API. Belarus carries no row more recent than 2019 in that dataset, so this is the latest published figure it offers, not a current one. The year field carries that and must be read with the value: the figure is sourced, it is simply 7 years old. The previous value was an opening estimate made with no source and no research. A national statistical office would give something fresher and has not been opened here.

Collected on 2026-07-28, in Belarusian and Russian, in the transversal venues pass. Seven units, seven houses, against an opening estimate of 5 produced with no research. The record was opened expecting to settle for secondary sources and a declared confidence, because this is the country where the schools layer stopped for want of anything first-party — Belarus is still the one disputed schools record in the series, no accessible source reaching stream level. That expectation was wrong, and the correction is worth stating: the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Belarus publishes its own register of theatres, republican level and local level, and the register names seven puppet theatres and no eighth. The Belarusian state puppet theatre in Minsk, on Enhelsa street, is the republican one and the oldest, founded on 15 July 1938 in Homiel as the state puppet theatre of the BSSR. The six others are the oblast network as the Soviet system laid it down and as it has stayed: Brest on Lenin street, Homiel on Pushkin 14, Hrodna on Dziarzhynski, Mahilioŭ on Pershamayskaya 73 in the building it has held since 1979, Viciebsk where the Belarusian theatre Lialka has worked since 1990, and the Minsk oblast theatre Batleyka at Maladzyechna rather than in the capital, its name being the Belarusian word for the nativity puppet box. Four of the seven carry the title of заслужаны калектыў Рэспублікі Беларусь. Every one is a freestanding institution whose vocation is puppetry, so seven houses and no stage, and the ministry's register is the backing itself rather than an inference about it. What was not done is a reading of each theatre's own pages: the addresses here come from the OpenStreetMap gazetteer queried on the theatres' names in Belarusian, and each point falls inside the country, but the register gives a city and a link and no street. The Brest, Hrodna and Mahilioŭ sites were not opened, so no founding decree or seat count is recorded for them, and a private field, if one exists, was not looked for at all. That is why the record is disputed and the upper bound is 8.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. Taken up again after too hasty a first reading. Value kept at 0 and status disputed. The Belarusian State Academy of Arts in Minsk is a state institution and did carry a Puppet Theatre Actor specialism: the encyclopaedic entry read dates the first intake to 1975 and a second, by distance learning, to 1987. A search summary further asserts the course is still active, on site and by distance. That assertion did not survive checking: the two admissions portals consulted and read list, at specialism level, only Acting and Theatre Directing, with no visible puppetry stream. This does not prove the course is gone, since the Belarusian system distinguishes the specialism from the stream within it and these portals do not descend to the second level; it proves only that no accessible source establishes it. Counting 1 would mean inferring from a 1975 intake the existence of a course in 2026, which the indicator's known bias forbids. The previous value of 1 was in any case an estimate made without research. To be checked by a route that reaches stream level: the ministry's official catalogue of specialisms, or direct contact with the academy's admissions board. The least satisfactory file in this pass.

establishments.description: The Belarusian State Academy of Arts enrolled its first puppet acting cohort in 1975 and a distance-learning cohort in 1987. Whether the stream still runs could not be established: published listings stop one level above where the answer would be.
